item.title: Central North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ACPN50 PHFO 270506
TWOCP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 PM HST Wed Aug 26 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Lala, located several hundred miles north of Kure Atoll. The
National Hurricane Center has issued the last advisory on
Post-Tropical Cyclone Iselle, located about 1000 miles west of the
southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula.

Western East Pacific (EP94):
An area of low pressure located well east-southeast of the Hawaiian
Islands continues to produce disorganized showers and thunderstorms.
Environmental conditions appear conducive for gradual development,
and a tropical depression is likely to form over the next two or
three days while the system drifts to the northeast, before turning
westward this weekend.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...medium...60 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...80 percent.

Central Pacific:
An area of low pressure could form well south of the Hawaiian
Islands over the weekend or early next week. Some gradual
development is possible thereafter while the system moves slowly
west-northwestward, well south-southwest of the Hawaiian Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

$$
Forecaster Cangialosi
NNNN

item.title: Tropical Storm Lala Public Advisory Number 60
item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM HST Wed Aug 26 2026 
000
WTPA32 PHFO 270843
TCPCP2
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Lala Advisory Number  60
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM HST Wed Aug 26 2026
 
...LALA DRIFTING NORTHWARD...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1100 PM HST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...37.0N 178.3W
ABOUT 595 MI...955 KM N OF KURE ATOLL
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...45 MPH...75 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...N OR 360 DEGREES AT 6 MPH...9 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...999 MB...29.50 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 PM HST (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Lala was 
located near latitude 37.0 North, longitude 178.3 West. Lala is 
moving toward the north near 6 mph (9 km/h). A northward to 
north-northwestward motion is expected through Thursday, followed by 
a gradual turn toward the west-northwest Thursday night and Friday. 
On the forecast track, Lala is forecast to cross the International 
Date line in about 30 to 36 h. 
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 45 mph (75 km/h) with higher gusts. 
Gradual weakening is expected during the next couple of days, and 
Lala is forecast to become a post-tropical remnant low Thursday 
night or Friday morning. 
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 125 miles (205 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 999 mb (29.50 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 500 AM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Adams

item.title: Tropical Storm Lala Forecast Discussion Number 60
item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM HST Wed Aug 26 2026 
502 
WTPA42 PHFO 270844
TCDCP2
 
Tropical Storm Lala Discussion Number  60
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI   CP012026
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM HST Wed Aug 26 2026
 
Mid-level dry air is beginning to wrap around the core of Lala, 
although a small area of deep convection persists near the center. 
An earlier AMSR-2 microwave pass indicated that moderate westerly 
wind shear is starting to take its toll, with a more defined 
circulation to the north and east of the center, and less definition 
on the southern and western sides. Subjective Dvorak intensity 
estimates from PHFO and JTWC were 2.0/30 kt, while objective 
intensity estimates from UW-CIMSS range from 47-55 kt. The initial 
intensity is maintained at 40 kt for this advisory.
 
Lala is moving northward around 5 kt, steered by a ridge of high 
pressure centered to the northeast of the storm. A northward to 
northwestward motion is expected over the next 24 h, followed by a 
turn toward the west-northwest as Lala approaches and crosses the 
International Date Line. Increasing wind shear and drier mid-level 
air will support gradual weakening over the next couple of days, and 
Lala may struggle to sustain deep, organized convection by late 
Thursday night or early Friday morning. The latest NHC track 
forecast has been shifted slightly to the right of the previous 
forecast and calls for Lala to become a post-tropical low by 36 h. 
The remnants of Lala should then gradually spin down and degenerate 
into a trough within about 3 days.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  27/0900Z 37.0N 178.3W   40 KT  45 MPH
